title: ZKnowledgeCompounding P0 深挖：半自动蒸馏（T3.1）与 LLM 编排/本地化（T3.3）
summary: 评估 6 个直接对应 T3.1/T3.3 的候选：Ollama、LiteLLM、LangGraph、Argilla、Instructor、Langfuse。结论：MVP 采用 Ollama（本地/离线推理）+ Instructor（结构化抽取与校验重试）+ LangGraph（编排 + 人审中断/恢复 + Postgres checkpoint，与已定 substrate 同库）；provider 统一收敛到 Instructor 接口以保留切云能力。延后 LiteLLM、Argilla、Langfuse。关键提醒：没有任何候选提供 ZKC 的蒸馏语义（去繁 → 元认知 + topic + 反向连接），管线原语之外的语义必须由 ZKC 自建。

concepts.value: Select the LLM orchestration and semi-automatic distillation stack for ZKC (T3.1 human-in-the-loop distillation, T3.3 LLM orchestration and localization) under privacy/offline and low-dependency constraints.
Coverage scored native / adapted / absent / unknown per topic; an unobserved capability is reported as unknown, never as absent. Sealed-ledger unknowns are footnoted rather than silently resolved.
Candidates supply pipeline primitives only. ZKC owns the distillation semantics (去繁 → 元认知 + topic + 反向连接), the review policy, and the quality rubric.
problem-discovery / selection phase for the ZKC LLM stack; findings are point-in-time and pre-MVP.

cards.title: Ollama — local model runtime
cards.summary: Runs open models locally/offline (llama.cpp GGUF + MLX safetensors), local REST API on :11434 plus OpenAI-compatible layer, tool calling and structured output, CUDA/ROCm/Vulkan/CPU/MLX. This is the piece that makes a fully private, offline distillation pipeline possible.

cards.title: LiteLLM — multi-provider AI gateway
cards.summary: Unifies 100+ LLM APIs in OpenAI format with routing, fallbacks, retries, cost tracking, guardrails and logging; supports local endpoints (Ollama, vLLM). Powerful, but its proxy requires PostgreSQL and adds a service — closer to infrastructure than to a distillation primitive.

cards.title: LangGraph — orchestration runtime with human-in-the-loop
cards.summary: Low-level runtime for stateful, long-running agents: durable execution (checkpoint/resume), human-in-the-loop (inspect and modify state mid-execution), memory, and a Postgres checkpoint backend. This is the natural seam for ZKC's 'distill → pause → human confirms → continue' loop, and it shares the chosen Postgres substrate.

cards.title: Argilla — human annotation / review platform
cards.summary: Open-source human-feedback tool (Apache 2.0) with Dataset/Settings/Fields/Questions/Records, record status, filters, semantic search and AI suggestions; self-hosted with PostgreSQL + Redis. Rich review UI, but heavy for MVP and the sealed evidence could not verify its human-in-the-loop criterion.

cards.title: Instructor — structured extraction primitive
cards.summary: Turns LLM output into validated Pydantic objects with automatic retries on validation failure, streaming partials and nested models, across a unified provider interface that includes local Ollama. This is the closest thing to a distillation primitive (text → validated structured claim).

cards.title: Langfuse — evals and observability
cards.summary: Open-source trace/evaluate/improve platform: traces, generation facts, token/cost accounting, score configs, evaluation rules, dataset items, LLM-based trace clustering (Topics). Self-hostable but brings ClickHouse/Redis/Node; the sealed evidence could not verify several of its criteria.

claims.text: Ollama runs open models locally and offline: GGUF models are served by llama-server (built from upstream llama.cpp) and safetensors models by an MLX engine, exposed through a local REST API on localhost:11434 plus an OpenAI-compatible layer, with tool calling and structured output supported via dedicated tools/format/parser packages.

Ollama ships as Docker images and CLI/desktop installers; once a model is downloaded, inference runs locally with complete privacy and no external service, across NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm, Vulkan, CPU, and Apple MLX backends.

LiteLLM is an AI gateway (Rust core plus Python SDK) that unifies 100+ LLM APIs in OpenAI format and provides routing, load balancing, fallbacks, retries, cost tracking, guardrails and logging; it supports local/self-hosted endpoints (vLLM, Ollama), with deployments taggable as type 'local'.

LiteLLM's proxy is deployed as containerised gateway/backend/migration components with a metrics dashboard, and its Prisma datasource is pinned to PostgreSQL, so self-hosting adds a database dependency beyond the model runtime.

LangGraph is a low-level orchestration runtime for long-running stateful agents that advertises durable execution (persist through failures and resume), human-in-the-loop (inspect and modify agent state at any point during execution), comprehensive memory, and production deployment; the project states it is consolidating as the runtime layer and that agent-building belongs on a separate harness.

LangGraph ships a Postgres checkpoint backend and a checkpoint-conformance suite, so workflow state for a distillation run can be durably persisted in the same PostgreSQL instance selected as the ZKC storage substrate.

Instructor produces structured, validated outputs from LLMs by declaring a Pydantic response model, with automatic retries on validation failure, streaming of partial objects, and nested object support; it advertises a unified provider interface so the same code runs across OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and local Ollama.

Instructor's unified provider interface is exposed as a provider/model string (for example 'ollama/...' or 'openai/...'), letting one extraction call path switch between a local runtime and hosted APIs without rewriting the response model.

Argilla is an open-source (Apache 2.0) human-feedback platform modelled as Dataset / Settings / Fields / Questions / Records with record status, offering filters, semantic search and AI feedback suggestions for reviewing LLM outputs; it is self-hosted (Docker Compose or Kubernetes) with a separate frontend, PostgreSQL and Redis. Note: the sealed ledger could not verify its human-in-the-loop criterion from the fetched evidence.

Langfuse is an open-source agent evals and observability platform (open-core with an enterprise directory) providing traces, generation-level facts (model, key owner, bytes, upstream errors), token/cost accounting, score configs, evaluation rules, dataset items, and LLM-based trace clustering; it is self-hostable via Docker. Note: the sealed ledger could not verify its orchestration, human-in-the-loop, or eval criteria from the fetched evidence.

None of the six candidates implements ZKC's distillation semantics (去繁 → 元认知 claim + topic 组织 + 基于元认知的反向连接); they supply pipeline primitives — extraction, orchestration, human interrupts, evaluation — while the transform semantics themselves remain ZKC's own work.

comparisons.text: T3.3 本地化：Ollama 是唯一原生本地推理运行时（下载后完全离线、隐私），且提供 OpenAI 兼容层；Instructor 通过 `ollama/...` provider 可直接调用它；LiteLLM 能把本地端点纳入路由（deployment type 'local'）但自身不是运行时。结论：本地化由 **Ollama** 承担，provider 抽象由 **Instructor 的统一接口**承担，二者组合即可满足 ZKC 的隐私/离线约束。

T3.3 编排：只有 LangGraph 提供真正的多步工作流编排（图 + 持久化 + 故障恢复 + 中断续跑），并有 Postgres checkpoint 后端——与已选定的 Postgres+pgvector substrate 同库，是显著协同。LiteLLM 只做单调用的路由/回退/重试，不是工作流引擎。结论：编排层选 **LangGraph**，并只用其明确的 runtime 原语（graph / checkpoint / interrupt-resume）。

T3.1 人审回路有两个层次：**工作流内中断**（LangGraph 的 human-in-the-loop，可在执行中检视并修改状态后恢复）适合「蒸馏过程中逐步确认」；**批量标注 UI**（Argilla）适合「事后集中审查」。MVP 应选前者——它与编排同源、无需额外服务；Argilla 需 PG+Redis 且处于维护模式，延后。注意 sealed ledger 未能验证 Argilla 的人审能力。

T3.1 蒸馏：Instructor 是唯一提供「文本 → 经过校验的结构化对象」的原语（Pydantic + 校验失败自动重试 + 嵌套 + 流式），这正是蒸馏出元认知 claim 所需的机械部分。但**没有任何候选提供 ZKC 的蒸馏语义**（去繁 → 元认知 + topic 组织 + 反向连接）。因此 Instructor 只是蒸馏管线里的抽取/校验原语，**语义必须 ZKC 自己定义并实现**。

评测/可观测：Langfuse 提供完整的 trace / score / eval-rules / dataset / Topics 聚类，但自带 ClickHouse + Redis + Node 栈，对单人 MVP 偏重，且 sealed ledger 未验证其核心 criteria。建议 MVP 先用一张轻量 score 表 + 蒸馏质量 rubric 自建最小度量，等评测需求真实增长再引入 Langfuse；LiteLLM 的 cost tracking 同理延后。

MVP 组合建议：**Ollama（本地推理）+ Instructor（结构化抽取与校验重试）+ LangGraph（编排 + 人审中断 + Postgres checkpoint）**，并把 provider 收敛到 Instructor 的统一接口以保持可切云。延后：LiteLLM（需 PG、MVP 不需要多 provider 路由）、Argilla（维护模式 + 重依赖）、Langfuse（重依赖，先自建轻量 score）。这与已定的 Postgres+pgvector substrate 高度协同（LangGraph 的 PG checkpoint 落在同一库）。

recommendations.text: 采用 **Ollama + Instructor + LangGraph** 作为 T3.1/T3.3 的 MVP 组合：Ollama 承担本地/离线推理（满足隐私约束），Instructor 承担「文本 → 校验过的结构化 claim」的蒸馏原语（含自动重试），LangGraph 承担多步编排与 human-in-the-loop 中断/恢复，并用其 **Postgres checkpoint 后端**落在已选定的 Postgres+pgvector 同一实例上。Provider 统一收敛到 Instructor 的 provider 接口，保留切云能力。**延后** LiteLLM（需 PostgreSQL、MVP 无需多 provider 路由）、Argilla（维护模式 + PG/Redis 重依赖）、Langfuse（ClickHouse/Redis 重依赖，先用轻量 score 表自建度量）。**关键提醒**：三者都不提供 ZKC 的蒸馏语义（去繁 → 元认知 + topic + 反向连接），该语义必须由 ZKC 自己定义并实现，它们只是管线原语。

动手验证清单：(1) **离线抽取 spike** —— 用 Instructor + Ollama 跑通「一条动态条目 → 结构化 claim」且全程无外部 API，记录校验重试率；(2) **人审回路 spike** —— 用 LangGraph 的 interrupt/resume 实现「蒸馏产出 → 暂停 → 人工确认/修改 → 继续」的最小闭环，并把状态持久化到 Postgres；(3) **质量基线** —— 定义蒸馏质量 rubric（准确性/去繁程度/可复用性），落地一张最小 score 表，作为后续是否引入 Langfuse 的判断依据。

riskRegister.risk: Local open-weight models served by Ollama may be too weak for high-quality distillation into meta-cognition.
riskRegister.trigger: Running the whole distillation pipeline offline on small local models.
riskRegister.impact: Distilled claims are low quality and the human review burden rises instead of falling.
riskRegister.mitigation: Benchmark a local model against a hosted model on a fixed 50-item distillation set, and keep the provider seam so the meta-cognition step can use the stronger model while routine extraction stays local.
riskRegister.residualRisk: A quality gap may persist for the hardest items even with routing.

riskRegister.risk: LangGraph is consolidating into the runtime layer and explicitly moves agent-building to a separate harness, so its convenience surface may shift.
riskRegister.trigger: Building the distillation workflow on LangGraph's higher-level agent conveniences.
riskRegister.impact: Rework when conveniences are deprecated or moved.
riskRegister.mitigation: Use only the primitives the project names as its consolidation target (graph, checkpointing, interrupt/resume) and pin the dependency version.
riskRegister.residualRisk: Even runtime-level APIs can change across major versions.

riskRegister.risk: Argilla is in maintenance mode (no new features, seeking maintainers) and requires PostgreSQL plus Redis.
riskRegister.trigger: Depending on Argilla for the human review UI in the MVP.
riskRegister.impact: A stale dependency plus extra infrastructure for a solo project.
riskRegister.mitigation: Defer Argilla and implement the review step as a LangGraph interrupt plus a thin in-app queue, revisiting only when annotation volume justifies it.
riskRegister.residualRisk: Migrating to a dedicated annotation tool later still costs effort.

riskRegister.risk: LiteLLM's proxy requires PostgreSQL and adds a service, so adopting it prematurely inflates the MVP's infrastructure.
riskRegister.trigger: Adding LiteLLM as the provider gateway before routing is needed.
riskRegister.impact: Operational surface grows beyond the chosen substrate for no MVP benefit.
riskRegister.mitigation: Use Instructor's unified provider interface as the seam and introduce LiteLLM only when multi-provider routing, fallbacks or cost tracking become real requirements.
riskRegister.residualRisk: Re-plumbing the provider layer later if routing is eventually needed.

riskRegister.risk: Treating structured extraction as if it were ZKC's distillation would leave the meta-cognition, topic organisation and reverse-link logic unbuilt.
riskRegister.trigger: Labelling Instructor's schema extraction as 'the distillation' and shipping it.
riskRegister.impact: ZKC's core compounding transform is never actually implemented.
riskRegister.mitigation: Write down the distillation contract (去繁 → 元认知 claim + topic + 反向连接) as ZKC-owned code and tests, and use Instructor only as the extraction and validation primitive inside it.
riskRegister.residualRisk: Semantic drift if the contract is not documented and covered by tests.

informationGaps.rationale: Has information gaps: the sealed ledger left 10 criteria unknown, notably human_in_the_loop for litellm, argilla and langfuse, orchestration for argilla and langfuse, and structured_extraction and eval_observability for argilla; those cells rest on documentation inspection and require hands-on validation before they are treated as verified.
